items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: It was he and I and Arthur Schutt and Jimmy Dorsey playing clarinet... That's right, I worked with him.

ctx.x: He used to talk about a lot, and how much he admired him.

Yes, Adrian did a date under the name of the California Ramblers, and I think -- was it that one, or -- no, it was one of those Brunswick dates, and that I did with him. That's right, I worked with him. It was one of those groups. It was he and I and Arthur Schutt and Jimmy Dorsey playing clarinet and if I'm not mistaken, Manny Klein. You'd just go in and play the popular tunes of the day, and -- and then I used him on vibraphones on one date that I did for the Irving Mills thing. I think that was a California…

items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: I'm not sure, I think Hal Kemp was already gone from the Taft, but George Hall. And oh, there were -- this was before Shaw started his thing and it was before the Dorseys. The Dorseys, I think -- the Dorsey Brothers, that year, I think they came the following year...

ctx.x: What other bands were playing in New York then, when you were there?

Well, at that time, let's see, the Casa Loma Band had come into the Roseland Ballroom and made quite a hit. Claude Hopkins' band was playing there also. And let's see, well, the inevitable Phil Spitalny and of course Freddie Martin, and Vincent Lopez. Let's see, I'm not sure, I think Hal Kemp was already gone from the Taft, but George Hall.
